purpose: Test whether the TES circuit inductance range used by the Elmer transient model can absorb the continuum residual that otherwise requires phenomenological c2. Scan fixed L from the historical noise-model scale through the Elmer-configured 12.3 nH value and beyond, comparing c2=0 and c2-free under the same relaxed thermal-backbone profile.

elmer_reference.semantics: This is the circuit inductance configured as an input to the Elmer TES branch. It is not an inductance inferred independently by Elmer.

guardrail: The fixed-L rows are sensitivity tests, not an inductance measurement or confidence interval. The Elmer 12.3 nH value is a configured circuit input, not an independent electromagnetic estimate. Each nominal fixed L is implemented as an extremely narrow +/-1e-6 relative profile solely to reuse the existing relaxed-thermal optimizer without changing its physics or parameter bookkeeping. A high-L row that improves the normalized noise fit does not by itself establish that the physical TES circuit has that inductance.
